sources.firmware: fn-h89 branch h89-disk-fixes @ 7ab84ae64, BUILD_RS232 + PINMAP_H89 (ESP32 card) / fujinet-pc FUJINET_TARGET=RS232

dispatch: fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/rs232.cpp:92-136 - service loop reads one SLIP frame, looks the device byte up in the daisy chain and calls its rs232_process(); an unregistered device byte gets a NAK (rs232.cpp:126-133)

fn-h89/lib/device/rs232/rs232Fuji.cpp:26,59-61 - eight rs232Network objects registered as 0x71..0x78 (MAX_NETWORK_DEVICES = 8, fn-h89/lib/device/fujiDevice/fujiDevice.h:21); every unit has its own channel, parser, prefix, login, password, EOL override, translation override and timer rate (fn-h89/lib/device/NDevice/NDevice.h:78-115)
fn-h89/lib/device/rs232/rs232Network.h:9 - rs232_process() forwards straight to NDevice::processCommand()
fn-h89/lib/device/NDevice/NDevice.cpp:97-115 - processCommand() looks the command byte up in the static dispatch_table; not found -> transaction_error() = NAK

fn-h89/lib/device/NDevice/NDevice.cpp:32-68 - dispatch_table: 29 commands (OPEN, CLOSE, READ, WRITE, STATUS, PARSE, QUERY, SET_PARAMETER, SET_PARSER, TRANSLATION, SET_EOL, SET_INT_RATE, SEEK, TELL, GETCWD, CHDIR, USERNAME, PASSWORD, RENAME, DELETE, LOCK, UNLOCK, MKDIR, RMDIR, ACCEPT, CLOSE_CLIENT, SET_HTTP_MODE, GET_REMOTE, SET_DESTINATION)
fn-h89/lib/device/rs232/rs232Network.cpp:6-15 - the only RS232-specific override: NET_QUERY takes the whole packet payload as the query (no 256-byte cap, no NUL truncation)

fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/rs232.cpp:173-202 - after every command/idle pass each unit's poll_interrupt() runs (protocol status side effects happen in the background); ESP32 drives RI, which on the H89 PPI channel is a no-op (fn-h89/lib/hardware/PPIChannel.h:48); fujinet-pc drives DTR or RTS per config, nothing under BoIP
packet_rules: fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/FujiBusPacket.cpp:55-95 - SLIP: frame is C0 <body> C0; inside the body C0 is sent as DB DC and DB as DB DD; an unknown escape pair is dropped

fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/rs232.cpp:337-359 - the firmware takes the first C0 as frame start and the next C0 as frame end; a doubled C0 at frame start yields an empty frame (dropped) and desynchronises the rest
fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/rs232.cpp:99-107 - bytes that arrive before a frame's opening C0 are handed to the modem (R:) device's tx(), not discarded
fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/FujiBusPacket.cpp:17-23 - 6-byte header: device, command, length (u16 little-endian, total decoded length including header), checksum, first descriptor
fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/FujiBusPacket.cpp:150-176 + rs232.cpp:111-116 - frame shorter than 8 raw bytes, length field != decoded size, or bad checksum -> packet silently dropped: NO reply at all

fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/FujiBusPacket.cpp:126-137 - checksum: 8-bit sum with end-around carry over every decoded byte, checksum byte taken as 0 (fujinet-lib/bus/h89/fuji_bus_call.c:56-65 computes the same)
fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/FujiBusPacket.cpp:28-35,203-208 - descriptor low 3 bits: 0 none, 1..4 = that many u8 fields, 5 = one u16, 6 = two u16, 7 = one u32

fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/FujiBusPacket.cpp:187-198 - descriptor bit 7 set: another descriptor byte follows the header (chained descriptors precede all field bytes); bits 3-6 are ignored - fujinet-lib puts its FUJI_FIELD_DATA (0x08) and FUJI_FIELD_REPLY (0x10) flags there on the wire (fujinet-lib/include/fujinet-bus-ezcall.h:16-17, fujinet-lib/bus/h89/fuji_bus_call.c:201)
fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/FujiBusPacket.cpp:210-226 - field values little-endian, in descriptor order; every byte after the last field is the payload (there is no separate payload length)

fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/FujiBusPacket.h:75-77 - handlers read fields by POSITION with _params.at(n); a missing field throws std::out_of_range and nothing catches it (no try/catch in lib/bus, lib/device, src). ESP32 H89 build has C++ exceptions disabled (fn-h89/sdkconfig.fujinet-heathkit-h89:422) -> abort -> panic/reboot; fujinet-pc -> std::terminate (process dies)
fn-h89/lib/device/NDevice/NDevice.h:31-44 - field WIDTH is not checked: the handler casts whatever value arrived to the type it wants (u8 for modes, u16 for lengths, u32 for SEEK)
fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/rs232.cpp:66-82 - payload copy (transaction_get) copies min(payload, handler buffer) and succeeds even if the payload is short; it fails only if the packet has no payload at all

fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/rs232.cpp:379-399 - reply packet: device = unit ID, command 0x06 ACK or 0x15 NAK, descriptor 0, no fields; ACK may carry a payload, NAK never does (data is dropped when ack is false)

fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/rs232.cpp:60-64 + rs232.cpp:126-133 - unknown device byte: NAK sent with whatever id() a null device yields (0x00), which fujinet-lib rejects as device mismatch (fujinet-lib/bus/h89/fuji_bus_call.c:149-156)

fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/rs232.h:23-25 + fn-h89/include/pinmap/heathkit_h89.h - on the ESP32 H89 card the link is the 82C55 at port 0xD0 (FUJINET_OVER_PPI); fujinet-pc uses a serial port or BoIP (rs232.cpp:216-244)
fn-h89/lib/bus/rs232/rs232.h:165 - computer-side (native) line ending on this bus is CR LF (0x0D 0x0A); used by OPEN spec trimming and by translation

fujinet-lib/bus/h89/fuji_bus_call.c:14,106-108 + port_slip.c:39-102 - client side: reply is accepted if its header length equals the bytes received; a reply SHORTER than the caller's buffer is accepted silently, a reply LONGER than the buffer fails (receive stops when the buffer is full); 15 s of silence (per character) = timeout

commands.name: NET_OPEN

fields.name: aux1 / mode
fields.meaning: access mode, see open_modes (cast to u8, NDevice.cpp:136)

fields.name: aux2 / trans
fields.meaning: translation mode for file/stream opens (see translation_modes); directory listing format when aux1 is 6 or 7 (see directory_formats)

payload.len: first 256 bytes used; longer payload silently truncated (NDevice.cpp:139-141)
payload.format: devicespec ASCII, e.g. 'N:HTTPS://host/path'. Cut at the first NUL, then at the first CR LF pair - a lone CR or LF is NOT removed (NDevice.cpp:23-30, native EOL rs232.h:165). Optional 'N:', 'n:' or 'N<digits>:' prefix stripped, digit ignored - the packet's device byte picks the unit (fn-h89/lib/utils/utils.cpp:883-910). A spec without its own 'SCHEME:' is appended to the unit prefix set by NET_CHDIR (utils.cpp:942-943). Then bytes >0x7F become NUL (utils.cpp:848-854,949), '*' becomes NUL unless aux1 is 6/7 (utils.cpp:953), one trailing '.' is removed (utils.cpp:957-960), trailing spaces removed (utils.cpp:840-846,963). Scheme compared case-insensitively (NetworkProtocolFactory.cpp:37). A valid URL needs a scheme (peoples_url_parser.cpp:333-339).

naks_when: no payload at all - the channel already open stays open (NDevice.cpp:141-146)
spec has no scheme -> STATUS err 165 INVALID_DEVICESPEC (NDevice.cpp:157-164)
unknown scheme -> STATUS err 144 GENERAL, not 165 (NDevice.cpp:157-164, NDevice.cpp:500-506)
protocol open failed (connect refused, file not found, bad aux1 for HTTP ...) -> STATUS err = protocol error (NDevice.cpp:178-186)

commands.side_effects: Closes a channel already open on the unit first, ignoring that close's result; this happens before the new spec is parsed, so even a failed OPEN loses the old channel (NDevice.cpp:150-157). Parser reset to NONE (NDevice.cpp:154,188); closeFailed cleared. Protocol native_eol set from NET_SET_EOL override or CR LF (NDevice.cpp:508, NDevice.cpp:127-130). For non-directory opens aux2 is ORed with the NET_TRANSLATION override; override 0xFF forces translation off (NDevice.cpp:169-176). HTTP opens do not send the request: GET/POST/DELETE go out on the first STATUS or READ (HTTP.cpp:430-436, 505-506), PUT at CLOSE (HTTP.cpp:553-554).
traps: Two fields are mandatory even when aux2 is 0; one field (or a single u16) crashes the firmware (NDevice.cpp:136-137, FujiBusPacket.h:75-77)
On TNFS:// and SD:// an aux1 other than 4/6/7/8/9/12 reaches abort() - firmware reboot (fn-h89/lib/network-protocol/TNFS.cpp:54-56, SD.cpp:56-58)
A '*' in a non-directory URL (e.g. in an HTTP query string) is turned into NUL and truncates the URL (utils.cpp:953)
A URL ending in '.' loses the dot (utils.cpp:957-960)
Terminate the spec with NUL or CR LF; a lone CR stays inside the URL (NDevice.cpp:27-29)
HTTP aux1 4 and 8 URL-encode the path (so do not pre-encode); 5/9/12/13/14 send it verbatim (HTTP.cpp:310-316)
UDP OPEN without a port NAKs but leaves STATUS err = 1 (error never set) (UDP.cpp:50-54, NDevice.cpp:182)

fujinet_lib.sends: NETCALL_A1_A2_D(NETCMD_OPEN, unit, mode, trans, devicespec, strlen(devicespec)): two u8 fields + spec without NUL (NETWORK_OPEN_LEN = strlen on variable-length platforms, fujinet-lib/include/fujinet-network.h:109-113; H89 is variable-length, fujinet-lib/include/fujinet-bus.h:6-14)

fujinet_lib.mismatch: OPEN alone sends no DELETE; the request only goes out if the caller then STATUSes or READs (HTTP.cpp:430-436); CLOSE without that sends nothing (HTTP.cpp:557-564)

fujinet_lib.sends: unit = 1 for 'N:', else devicespec[1]-'0' when devicespec[2] is ':', else 1; device = 0x70 + unit (fujinet-lib/include/fujinet-bus-eznet.h:84-85)
fujinet_lib.mismatch: no range check: 'N9:' addresses 0x79, which is NAKed

commands.pc_vs_esp32: TCP connect: 5000 ms timeout on PC, fnTcpClient default (-1) on ESP32 (TCP.cpp:277-281, fn-h89/lib/tcpip/fnTcpClient.h:27). UDP bind differs (UDP.cpp:62-67). HTTP client class fnHttpClient (ESP32) vs mgHttpClient (PC) (HTTP.h:9-15). Missing-field crash: panic+reboot vs process exit.
commands.notes: aux1 is ignored by TCP/UDP (any value works; only 6/7 change how aux2 is used). Opening is synchronous: TCP connect, TNFS mount, FS stat/resolve all happen before the reply; the H89 library gives up after 15 s of silence (fujinet-lib/bus/h89/fuji_bus_call.c:14).

commands.name: NET_CLOSE

naks_when: the protocol's close() failed (HTTP PUT got an error status, upload failed, FS close error); STATUS then reports that error (NDevice.cpp:201-206)
every following CLOSE also NAKs until the next OPEN (NDevice.cpp:199-214)

commands.side_effects: Protocol close: bytes still in the transmit buffer are written first (Protocol.cpp:127-128); HTTP PUT is sent here (HTTP.cpp:553-554); FS file/dir close and unmount (FS.cpp:230-259). Parser discarded. Unit settings (prefix, login, password, EOL override, translation override, timer rate) are kept. With no channel open: ACK; this also clears an error left by a failed OPEN, so STATUS then reads 00 00 00 CF.
traps: HTTP POST (aux1 13/14) and DELETE (5/9) are never sent if no STATUS/READ happened before CLOSE: resultCode 0 means 'no transaction' and close just succeeds (HTTP.cpp:553-564)

commands.name: NET_READ

fields.name: length
fields.meaning: most bytes to return; any field width accepted, value taken as u16 (NDevice.cpp:235)

layout.name: data
layout.meaning: channel bytes, after aux2 translation; with a JSON/HTML/XML parser these are the bytes queued by NET_QUERY

naks_when: protocol read failed: FS file at EOF/nothing left (FS.cpp:303-312), TCP short socket read with empty buffer (TCP.cpp:123-139), UDP nothing waiting (UDP.cpp:106-112), HTTP short body read (HTTP.cpp:508-514), HTTP header-set modes err 131 (HTTP.cpp:478-482); after a failed OPEN/CLOSE (NParser.h:39)

commands.side_effects: Data read from the network passes through translation once (Protocol.cpp:146-154, FS.cpp:318-319, TCP.cpp:144-145); a translated surplus stays buffered for the next READ.
traps: TCP: READ with nothing pre-buffered asks the socket for exactly 'length'; a short read NAKs with err 202 and the bytes that did arrive are thrown away (TCP.cpp:123-139). Always STATUS first (it pre-reads into the buffer, Protocol.cpp:169-175) and ask for no more than bytes-waiting
HTTP body with nothing buffered: client read short -> NAK and the partial bytes are lost (HTTP.cpp:508-514, FS.cpp:303-312)
UDP with empty buffer pads the reply with zero bytes up to 'length' (UDP.cpp:102,115-118)

HTTP GET_HEADERS mode: each READ consumes one header and copies exactly 'length' bytes from it (over-read when length > header); a READ after the last header indexes past the vector - undefined, may crash (HTTP.cpp:490-495)
If NET_SET_PARSER was sent while no channel was open, READ dereferences a null protocol - crash (NDevice.cpp:543-561, NParser.cpp:5)

fujinet_lib.sends: NETCALL_B12_RV(NETCMD_READ, unit, length, buffer, length): one u16 field, reply into buffer
fujinet_lib.mismatch: returns 'length' for any ACK even when the firmware sent fewer bytes - fuji_packet_call only checks received == header length (fujinet-lib/bus/h89/fuji_bus_call.c:108); short replies are invisible

fujinet_lib.sends: STATUS polls until avail>0 (returns 0 if err>1 and nothing waiting), caps length to avail, then network_bus_read
fujinet_lib.mismatch: busy-loops forever while err==1 and avail==0 (e.g. UDP under-report, idle TCP server)

fujinet_lib.sends: loops network_read_nb until len satisfied or 0/negative

commands.pc_vs_esp32: same logic; socket/HTTP client timing differs
commands.notes: Rule for assembly programmers: STATUS, then READ min(want, bytes-waiting). The reply's header length tells how many bytes actually came.

commands.name: NET_WRITE

naks_when: JSON/HTML/XML parser set - parser write always fails (JSONParser.cpp:3-6, HTMLParser.cpp:3-6, XMLParser.cpp:3-6)
TCP not connected, err 207 (TCP.cpp:166-170); short send err 202 (TCP.cpp:184-189)

HTTP: BODY-mode write on anything but PUT err 132 (HTTP.cpp:677-687); GET_HEADERS mode err 135 (HTTP.cpp:596-598); SET_HEADERS text without ':' (HTTP.cpp:641-642); COLLECT_HEADERS on non-GET err 146 (HTTP.cpp:606-610); SET_POST_DATA on non-POST/PUT err 132 (HTTP.cpp:667-671)

commands.side_effects: Bytes are appended to the protocol transmit buffer, then translated (native EOL -> network EOL) and sent (NParser.cpp:14-21, FS.cpp:344-349, TCP.cpp:173, UDP.cpp:134). HTTP buffers PUT/POST bodies and request headers for later.
traps: Payload shorter than the length field: zero bytes are appended up to 'length' and written (NDevice.cpp:276-281, rs232.cpp:77-81); longer: the excess is ignored

A failed write leaves its bytes in the transmit buffer; they are prepended to the next WRITE and retried at CLOSE (FS.cpp:351-356, TCP.cpp:166-196, Protocol.cpp:127-128). NET_SET_HTTP_MODE clears the buffer (HTTP.cpp:69-70)
Write translation looks for the full native EOL (CR LF unless NET_SET_EOL changed it); a lone CR is not translated (Protocol.cpp:231, rs232.h:165)

A STATUS on an HTTP PUT channel before CLOSE fires the PUT early with the data so far (empty body -> client returns -1 -> err 144); CLOSE then PUTs again (HTTP.cpp:430-436, 553-554, fn-h89/lib/http/mgHttpClient.cpp:982-983)

fujinet_lib.sends: NETCALL_B12_D(NETCMD_WRITE, unit, length, buffer, length): one u16 field + payload
whole buffer in one packet (no chunking)
fujinet_lib.mismatch: header length is u16, so a single write must keep the packet under 65536 bytes
network_http_put is just network_http_post: it works for aux1 8 only because SET_POST_DATA accepts PUT too (HTTP.cpp:667)

commands.name: NET_STATUS

layout.name: avail
layout.meaning: bytes the next READ can return, u16 little-endian, capped at 65535 (NDevice.cpp:319)

layout.name: connected
layout.meaning: FS file: 1 while bytes remain (FS.cpp:394); FS dir: 1 while listing remains (FS.cpp:405); HTTP body: 1 until the HTTP transaction is finished (HTTP.cpp:441), 0 in header modes; TCP client: socket connected (TCP.cpp:217); TCP server with no accepted client: 1 if a client is waiting (TCP.cpp:227); UDP: always 1 (UDP.cpp:185)

layout.name: err
layout.meaning: NDEV_STATUS code (see error_codes): 1 OK, 136 end of data, others = failure reason

commands.side_effects: First STATUS on an HTTP channel in BODY mode performs the HTTP request and blocks until the response starts (HTTP.cpp:430-436). If the receive buffer is empty, data already available is pre-read into it for TCP, UDP, directory listings, and for FS/HTTP when translation is on (Protocol.cpp:162-178, FS.cpp:389-390, HTTP.cpp:438-439). UDP: replaces the send destination with the last datagram's sender (UDP.cpp:169-183). Resets the interrupt timer (NDevice.cpp:333,343).
traps: No channel: 00 00 00 CF (207 NOT_CONNECTED) (NDevice.cpp:309-314); after a failed OPEN or CLOSE: 00 00 00 <reason> (NParser.h:31-51)

UDP under-reports: STATUS pre-reads the waiting datagram into the receive buffer, then computes avail from udp.available() - the NEXT datagram - so a single pending datagram shows avail 0 (Protocol.cpp:169-175, NDevice.cpp:317-319, UDP.h:72, fn-h89/lib/tcpip/fnUDP.cpp:286-314). The datagram is still returned by a READ
err 136 appears as soon as an FS file or HTTP body is fully consumed, including right after a JSON PARSE (body consumed) and before QUERY fills the buffer (FS.cpp:398, HTTP.cpp:443-444)
After a failed PARSE err stays 213 (JSON) or 144 (HTML/XML) on every STATUS (NParser.cpp:58-59)
HTTP GET_HEADERS mode: STATUS (and the background interrupt poll via available()) fires the request if not done yet (HTTP.cpp:456-458, 959-961)

fujinet_lib.sends: NETCALL_RV(FUJICMD_STATUS = 0x53, unit, &nw_status, 4); NetworkStatus {u16 avail; u8 status; u8 errcode} (fujinet-network.h:60-64) matches the firmware layout

commands.pc_vs_esp32: UDP status: ESP32 refreshes the destination whenever remoteIP != IPADDR_NONE, PC only when a datagram is waiting (UDP.cpp:174-178)

commands.name: NET_PARSE

naks_when: document does not parse or is empty -> err 213 for JSON (JSONParser.cpp:26-32, fn-h89/lib/fnjson/fnjson.cpp:381-393), err 144 for HTML/XML (HTMLParser.cpp:30, XMLParser.cpp:30)

commands.side_effects: JSON: frees the previous document, then reads the whole remaining stream into memory, looping while the protocol says connected or has bytes (fnjson.cpp:347-377) - for HTTP this performs the request. The body is consumed: afterwards READ returns only NET_QUERY results.
traps: On a stream that stays connected (e.g. TCP) PARSE does not return until the peer disconnects (fnjson.cpp:364); the H89 library times out after 15 s of silence (fujinet-lib/bus/h89/fuji_bus_call.c:14)

fujinet_lib.sends: SET_PARSER fields (1,1) then PARSE with no fields

commands.pc_vs_esp32: ESP32 yields 10 ticks per loop pass (fnjson.cpp:374-376)

commands.name: NET_QUERY

payload.len: any; the whole payload is the query, no 256-byte cap, no NUL truncation, no text conversion (rs232Network.cpp:9)
payload.format: JSON: JSON Pointer (RFC 6901), e.g. '/data/0/name', resolved with cJSONUtils_GetPointer on the C string, so anything after a NUL is ignored; empty = whole document (fnjson.cpp:120-126). HTML: CSS selector with optional '@attr' suffix (fn-h89/lib/fnhtml/fnhtml.cpp:106-112). XML: XPath subset (NDevice.h:23). HTML/XML: sending the identical query string again returns the next match (fnhtml.cpp:80-88, fn-h89/lib/fnxml/fnxml.cpp:83-91). No payload = empty query.

naks_when: JSON path not found is NOT an error: ACK and nothing is queued (fnjson.cpp:320-321,332-335; JSONParser.cpp:13-24 ignores readValue's result)

commands.side_effects: The formatted value is APPENDED to the receive buffer (JSONParser.cpp:23): read it with STATUS (avail = length) then READ. Unread results accumulate. JSON formatting (fnjson.cpp:209-313): string = text + line ending; integer-valued number as integer, else up to 10 significant digits; true/false -> TRUE/FALSE; null -> NULL; object -> for each member: key, line ending, value (recursive); array -> each element's value. Line ending default 0x0A (JSONParser.h:15), changed with NET_SET_PARAMETER 1. Value cut at an embedded NUL (JSONParser.cpp:20). aux2 translation is NOT applied to query output. Query flags (NET_SET_PARAMETER 0): 0x04 strip <tags>, 0x10 ASCII output mode (fnjson.cpp:131-151); 0x01/0x02 character remaps are compiled only for Atari (fnjson.cpp:162-201).
traps: Querying a value that is, or contains, an empty array [] crashes the firmware: the array loop dereferences a null child (fnjson.cpp:301-307). Any query whose result includes [] - including the empty query on a document containing [] - triggers it
Flag 0x04 with a string holding '<' but no later '>' loops forever (fnjson.cpp:135-144)

HTML/XML: the RS232 handler keeps a trailing NUL and any bytes after it in the selector string (rs232Network.cpp:9; fnhtml.cpp:80-112 compares/parses the whole std::string) - send exactly the selector bytes
NET_SET_PARSER while no channel was open, then QUERY -> null protocol dereference crash (JSONParser.cpp:23)

fujinet_lib.sends: NETCALL_D(NETCMD_QUERY, unit, query, MAX_JSON_QUERY_LEN = 256) then STATUS/READ until avail==0, then strips trailing 0x9B/CR/LF and NUL-terminates (fujinet-lib/common/network_json.c:6-20)
fujinet_lib.mismatch: always sends 256 bytes whatever strlen(query) is (reads past short query strings; a query of 256+ chars is truncated); harmless for JSON (firmware stops at NUL) but corrupts HTML/XML selectors. The READ loop has no buffer limit: a value longer than the caller's buffer overflows it, and the terminating NUL needs one more byte
inherits the 256-byte send -> selector gets NUL + garbage on RS232

commands.notes: Typical sequence: OPEN, SET_PARSER(1), [SET_PARAMETER], PARSE, then per value: QUERY, STATUS, READ avail bytes.

commands.name: NET_SET_PARAMETER

fields.name: param
fields.meaning: 0 = query flags, 1 = query line-ending character (NDevice.cpp:624-629, NDevice.h:26-29)
fields.if_missing: crash, but only when a parser exists - with none it NAKs before reading fields (NDevice.cpp:616-620)

fields.name: value
fields.meaning: param 0: flags, bits 0-2 remap/strip, bits 4-5 output mode 0x00 verbatim or 0x10 ASCII (fn-h89/lib/fntext/fn_query_flags.h:13-36); param 1: the line-ending byte

naks_when: param 0 with bits outside 0x37 or output mode 0x20/0x30 (fn_query_flags.h:29-36, NDevice.cpp:637-641)

commands.side_effects: param 1 with JSON/HTML/XML: sets the line ending appended to query values (single byte). With parser NONE it sets the protocol lineEnding, which is only used when an FS directory listing is built at OPEN (FS.cpp:90-92), so it has no visible effect afterwards.
traps: NET_SET_PARSER builds a fresh parser and resets flags and line ending: send SET_PARAMETER after SET_PARSER (NDevice.cpp:543-569, JSONParser.h:14-17)
param 1 with parser NONE after SET_PARSER-before-OPEN dereferences a null protocol (NParser.cpp:68-72)

commands.name: NET_SET_PARSER

fields.name: mode
fields.meaning: 0 NONE, 1 JSON, 2 HTML (CSS selectors), 3 XML (XPath subset) (NDevice.h:19-24)

commands.side_effects: Replaces the parser with a new instance over the current protocol (NDevice.cpp:543-569): earlier PARSE results, flags and line ending are gone. With JSON/HTML/XML set, WRITE always NAKs and SEEK fails.
traps: Does not check for an open channel: with none it creates a parser bound to a null protocol, and a later READ, QUERY, SEEK/TELL (mode 0) or SET_PARAMETER 1 (mode 0) crashes the firmware (NDevice.cpp:548-561, NParser.cpp:5,33,70, JSONParser.cpp:23)
OPEN resets the parser to NONE (NDevice.cpp:154,188): send SET_PARSER after OPEN
Write HTTP POST data before switching to JSON - writes NAK afterwards (JSONParser.cpp:3-6)

commands.name: NET_TRANSLATION
commands.side_effects: Stores a per-unit override. It does NOT change the channel already open; each later non-directory OPEN ORs it into aux2 (NDevice.cpp:172-176). 0xFF makes later OPENs use no translation whatever aux2 says (NDevice.cpp:170-171). Persists until changed.
traps: OR semantics: override 1 with aux2 2 gives mode 3 (CR LF) (NDevice.cpp:174)

commands.name: NET_SET_EOL

payload.format: raw bytes that become the computer-side line ending used by translation; NOT NUL-trimmed. Empty/no payload restores the default CR LF (NDevice.cpp:604-607, NDevice.cpp:127-130)

naks_when: never on RS232 (varlen read cannot fail here, fn-h89/lib/bus/bus.h:94-123)

commands.side_effects: Applies at once to the open protocol and to later opens (NDevice.cpp:608-610, NDevice.cpp:508).
traps: A NUL terminator in the payload becomes part of the line ending

fujinet_lib.sends: NETCALL_VLD -> DEVCALL_D with strlen(eol) bytes, or DEVCALL with no data for '' (fujinet-lib/common/fuji_devcall_vld.c:10-14)

commands.notes: For an H89 program that ends lines with a bare CR, SET_EOL 0x0D makes mode 2/3 translation map CR<->LF / CR<->CR LF.

commands.name: NET_SET_INT_RATE
commands.side_effects: Sets timerRate (default 100 ms ESP32, 20 ms PC, NDevice.h:72-76) used by poll_interrupt to pace the data-ready signal (NDevice.cpp:859-884).
traps: rate 0: poll_interrupt divides by timerRate*2 - integer division by zero, firmware crash once a channel is open on that unit (NDevice.cpp:861,867); poll_interrupt runs on the H89 card too (rs232.cpp:173-183)

On the H89 card the data-ready signal goes nowhere: ESP32 calls setRI(), a no-op on PPIChannel (rs232.cpp:186-187, PPIChannel.h:48); fujinet-pc drives DTR/RTS only on a real serial port with serial_proceed configured, never under BoIP (rs232.cpp:184-199)

fujinet_lib.mismatch: comment says RS232 reads aux2; firmware reads field 0 - harmless since both carry rate

commands.name: NET_SEEK

fields.name: offset
fields.meaning: absolute byte position (SEEK_SET only), u32; narrower field widths also accepted (NDevice.cpp:686)

commands.name: NET_GETCWD

reply.len: length of the unit prefix (0 when unset)

commands.name: NET_CHDIR

payload.format: path, cut at the first NUL only (NDevice.cpp:416-420); optional N:/Nn: stripped (NDevice.cpp:355). Rules (NDevice.cpp:358-408): empty -> clear prefix; contains ':' (SCHEME://...) -> replace; '/path' -> keep SCHEME://host, replace path; '..' or '<' -> up one level; '/' or '>' -> back to the host root; anything else -> appended. A trailing '/' is added and the result canonicalised.

commands.side_effects: Updates the unit prefix used by later OPEN and fs commands whose spec has no scheme (utils.cpp:942-943). Does not touch the open channel and does not check that the directory exists.
traps: CR/LF are NOT stripped (unlike OPEN): a CR LF-terminated payload puts CR LF into the prefix and into every later relative OPEN (NDevice.cpp:420)
A packet with no payload clears the prefix (transaction_get failure ignored, NDevice.cpp:419)

fujinet_lib.sends: NETCALL_D(NETCMD_CHDIR, unit, devicespec, strlen(devicespec)) - no fields, spec incl. 'Nn:' and no NUL

commands.name: NET_USERNAME

payload.format: bare user name, cut at the first NUL; CR/LF kept (NDevice.cpp:516-519)

commands.side_effects: Stored per unit. Handed to a protocol when it is created (OPEN or fs command) only if non-empty; passed by pointer, so a change after OPEN is seen by the open protocol (NetworkProtocolFactory.cpp:125-129). No payload clears it.
traps: If the user name is empty the password is not passed either (NetworkProtocolFactory.cpp:125-129)

fujinet_lib.sends: NETCALL_A1_A2_D(NETCMD_USERNAME, unit, 0, 0, username, strlen) - two dummy fields (ignored) + name without NUL

commands.notes: URL userinfo (user:pass@host) is the alternative for schemes that parse it (e.g. IMAPS.h header, S3.h header).

commands.name: NET_PASSWORD

payload.format: bare password, cut at the first NUL; CR/LF kept (NDevice.cpp:525-528)

fields.name: mode

commands.name: NET_ACCEPT

naks_when: channel is not TCP or TELNET (NDevice.cpp:770-775)
channel is a TCP client, not a listener -> err 208 (TCP.cpp:297-302)

commands.side_effects: The waiting connection becomes the channel's client socket; READ/WRITE/STATUS now act on it (TCP.cpp:205-231, 310-319). Server keeps listening.
traps: Poll STATUS first: on a listener with no client 'connected' = 1 means a client is waiting (TCP.cpp:225-229)
commands.notes: Listener: OPEN 'N:TCP://:port' (no host) (TCP.cpp:61-66); client: 'N:TCP://host:port', port defaults to 23 (TCP.cpp:72-78).

commands.name: NET_CLOSE_CLIENT

naks_when: INVERTED: it NAKs when it actually disconnected the client (close_client_connection returns UNSPECIFIED on success, TCP.cpp:357-370)

commands.side_effects: Clears receive/transmit/special buffers and stops the client socket; listener stays up (TCP.cpp:363-368). When there is nothing to do it ACKs and sets err 208 (no listener) or 207 (no client) (TCP.cpp:343-355).
traps: Return value inverted: NAK = client closed, ACK = nothing was closed (TCP.cpp:347,354,370)

fujinet_lib.mismatch: returns FN_ERR_IO_ERROR after a successful disconnect and FN_ERR_OK when nothing was connected (firmware inversion)

commands.name: NET_SET_HTTP_MODE

fields.name: unused

fields.name: mode
fields.meaning: HTTP channel mode 0-4, see http_channel_modes (NDevice.cpp:815, HTTP.h:22-28)
fields.if_missing: crash (only reached on an HTTP channel)

naks_when: channel is not HTTP/HTTPS - checked before the fields are read (NDevice.cpp:806-811)

commands.name: NET_GET_REMOTE

layout.name: remote
layout.meaning: ASCII 'a.b.c.d:port' of the last datagram's sender (UDP.cpp:230-232)

naks_when: channel is not UDP (NDevice.cpp:826-831); get_remote itself never fails (UDP.cpp:235)

commands.side_effects: Writes the text into the receive buffer's storage without resizing it.
traps: Overwrites the first ~22 bytes of an unread datagram, and writes past the string's allocation when the receive buffer is empty/small; then sends 256 bytes read from that storage (NDevice.cpp:834-835)
Before any datagram arrived the address is fnUDP's initial remote_ip/remote_port (fn-h89/lib/tcpip/fnUDP.cpp:349-357)

fujinet_lib.sends: NETCALL_RV(NETCMD_GET_REMOTE, unit, buf, len), then buf[len-1]=0 and strips trailing 0x9B/CR/LF

The header comment 'ESP32 firmware rejects it' (fujinet-network.h:438) is stale - this firmware dispatches it on every build (NDevice.cpp:66)

commands.name: NET_SET_DESTINATION

payload.format: 'N:host:port' - needs two colons: text between the first and last colon is the host, digits after the last colon the port (UDP.cpp:202-221)

commands.side_effects: Next WRITE goes to host:port (UDP.cpp:146-158).
traps: ESP32 extracts the host with substr(first_colon+1, last_colon-2), correct only when the first colon is at index 1: 'N:host:port' works, 'N1:host:port' yields 'host:' and sends fail (UDP.cpp:211-212)
fujinet-pc builds the string with strlen on a payload that is not NUL-terminated - send a trailing NUL (UDP.cpp:197-200, NDevice.cpp:847)
Any STATUS after a datagram arrives replaces the destination with that datagram's sender (UDP.cpp:169-183)

fujinet_lib.sends: NETCALL_VLD(NETCMD_SET_DESTINATION, unit, dest_spec, strlen) - no NUL
fujinet_lib.mismatch: its documented form 'N1:host:port' (fujinet-network.h:426) hits the ESP32 substr bug; the unit digit is needed to address units 2-8, so only unit 1 ('N:host:port') works on ESP32. No NUL for the PC strlen

open_modes.meaning: READ. FS: open for reading (TNFS.cpp:38-41). HTTP: GET; path URL-encoded, filename resolve (HTTP.cpp:114-117,310-316); request sent on first STATUS/READ. TCP/UDP: aux1 ignored.
HTTP DELETE, no headers (HTTP.cpp:121-124); sent on first STATUS/READ, never by CLOSE alone. On TNFS/SD: abort().
DIRECTORY. FS: listing built at OPEN, aux2 = listing format (FS.cpp:52-53,87-207). HTTP: WebDAV PROPFIND; 405/408 falls back to GET (HTTP.cpp:144-277).
DIRECTORY_ALT, same as 6 (IS_DIR_MODE, NDevice.cpp:19-21); HTTP strips '*.*' only for 6 (HTTP.cpp:304-308).

WRITE. FS: create/truncate (TNFS.cpp:42-45). HTTP: PUT, path URL-encoded; BODY-mode writes buffered and the PUT is sent at CLOSE (HTTP.cpp:118-120,677-683,553-554) - or early by any STATUS/READ (HTTP.cpp:430-436).
FS: APPEND (TNFS.cpp:46-49). HTTP: DELETE with headers allowed (HTTP.cpp:122-124).
FS: READWRITE (TNFS.cpp:50-53). HTTP: GET with request/response headers, path sent verbatim, no resolve (HTTP.cpp:115-117); the only mode where COLLECT_HEADERS works (HTTP.cpp:606,731).

HTTP POST: body written in SET_POST_DATA mode (4), then BODY mode (0) and STATUS/READ sends it (HTTP.cpp:125-128,665-675,742). Empty body -> client returns -1 -> err 144 (mgHttpClient.cpp:1120-1121, fnHttpClient.cpp:804-805).
HTTP 'PUT with headers' - BUG: normalised to POST, so a POST is sent (HTTP.cpp:125-128).

HTTP: NAK, err 146 (HTTP.cpp:129-131). TNFS/SD: abort() -> firmware reboot (TNFS.cpp:54-56, SD.cpp:56-58). NFS/SMB: logged, open proceeds with default flags (NFS.cpp:66-67, SMB.cpp:68-69). SFTP: fails (SFTP.cpp:289-291).

translation_modes.meaning: network side uses CR: reads replace each CR with the native EOL (CR LF unless NET_SET_EOL), writes replace native EOL with CR
network side uses LF: reads LF -> native EOL, writes native EOL -> LF
network side uses CR LF: with the default native EOL CR LF this is a no-op both ways
PETSCII <-> UTF-8 (Commodore); no EOL change; meaningless on H89
no translation for file/stream opens (netproto_is_translation_enabled checks 1..4)

Effective mode = aux2 OR NET_TRANSLATION override (0xFF override = none). Translation happens once, when bytes come off the network (Protocol.cpp:146-154 via TCP.cpp:145, UDP.cpp:122, FS.cpp:319, FS.cpp:339) and when written (FS.cpp:347, TCP.cpp:173, UDP.cpp:134). With translation on, FS/HTTP STATUS reads ahead up to 512 bytes so avail counts translated bytes (FS.cpp:30, Protocol.cpp:172-174). A CR LF split across two writes/reads is not matched. Directory opens use aux2 as the listing format, but aux2 1-4 still also enables translation of the listing (Protocol.cpp:115, FS.cpp:339).

directory_formats.meaning: short entries: RS232 build formats 'NAME     EXT       size  1-01-24 12:00p' (8.3 crunched name, size or <DIR>, fixed fake date) (fn-h89/lib/utils/utils.cpp:225-279, FS.cpp:171)
LONG: 37-column entries (dirLongWidth, Protocol.h:175), '/' after directory names, size as n/nK/n.nM; a name longer than 30 chars wraps with an embedded 0x9B (utils.cpp:328-370, FS.cpp:168-169)
GDRIVE: entry with Google Drive id (FS.cpp:154-156)
RAW: exact name, '/' appended for directories (FS.cpp:157-166)
ProDOS CAT / CATALOG with header and trailer (FS.cpp:123-134,182-194)
Lines end CR LF on non-Atari builds (FS.cpp:90-92); entries starting with '.' or '/' are skipped (FS.cpp:138-139); whole listing is built at OPEN and served from memory (FS.cpp:328-342)

http_channel_modes.name: BODY
http_channel_modes.meaning: READ returns the response body (request sent on first STATUS/READ); for PUT (aux1 8) WRITE appends to the body; bytes-remaining reset to body size

http_channel_modes.name: COLLECT_HEADERS
http_channel_modes.meaning: each WRITE registers one response-header name to capture; one trailing 0x9B/CR/LF is dropped; GET only (aux1 4 or 12) else err 146, and only aux1 12 actually captures (http_transaction ignores the list for aux1 4/8). Must precede the request.

http_channel_modes.name: GET_HEADERS
http_channel_modes.meaning: STATUS avail = length of the next captured value + 1; each READ returns one value followed by 0x9B; values come in alphabetical order of the lower-cased header name (std::map), not registration order; absent headers give an empty value; err 136 after the last. Entering this mode fires the request if not yet sent.

http_channel_modes.name: SET_HEADERS
http_channel_modes.meaning: each WRITE is one request header 'Name: value' - split at the first ':', value taken from 2 bytes after it (so exactly one space is expected), 0x9B and anything after it removed, no ':' -> NAK. fujinet-pc trims whitespace (incl. CR/LF) from name and value; ESP32 does not trim (a trailing CR LF stays in the value). Must precede the request.

http_channel_modes.name: SET_POST_DATA
http_channel_modes.meaning: WRITEs append to the request body for POST (13/14) and PUT (8); other methods err 132
